name: Apache HBase
model: Sparse sorted map: row key to column families of versioned cells; get, put, scan by row key range; no SQL without Phoenix
engine_note: Bigtable-style LSM: write-ahead log and memstore per region, flushed to HFiles on HDFS, compacted in the background
consistency: All mutations are atomic within one row (no multi-row transactions by default). Each row is served by one region server, so reads are strongly consistent and see every acknowledged write; optional region replicas give stale 'timeline' reads.
scaling: Tables split into regions by row key range automatically; regions spread over region servers and rebalanced; storage scales with the HDFS (or object store) cluster.
managed: Amazon EMR (HBase on S3 or HDFS)
version_note: 3.0.0 is the first 3.x GA (2026-08-05 per downloads page; GitHub release object 2026-08-06). The project still marks the 2.5 line 'stable release' (2.5.16 and 2.6.7 both 2026-10-01).
reach: Reach for it when you already run Hadoop/HDFS and need random reads and writes by row key over billions of rows with strong per-row consistency.
avoid: Avoid when you have no Hadoop stack, need secondary indexes, SQL or transactions out of the box, or a small team to operate ZooKeeper, HDFS and region servers.
escape: Data is billions of rows keyed by row and already lives in a Hadoop cluster.
chat: Nothing for a new chat app; maybe raw usage events in an existing Hadoop shop.
notes: HBase ACID semantics page: 'All mutations are atomic within a row' and 'All visible data is also durable data'. Default WAL durability in HBase is SYNC_WAL, which on HDFS means hflush to DataNodes' memory rather than fsync to disk (FSYNC_WAL is an option); from the reference guide, not re-read line by line here. Region replicas (timeline consistency) are off by default. No Jepsen report on HBase.
